identity.name: Sohail (Neel) Sarkar
identity.summary: AI & Statistics Researcher at the PMCC AI Lab, University Health Network, and Vector Institute. Applied mathematics and computer science student at the University of Toronto. Previously Applied AI at Lyft, Applied ML at Shopify, and Applied Scientist at Sigma Squared. Research spans statistical imaging, reliable LLM evaluation, and computational genomics, alongside sole-authored work in geometry and quantum learning.
affiliations: PMCC AI Lab, Peter Munk Cardiac Centre, University Health Network

bullets: Engineered a rider-history and offer-response cross-feature for a production LightGBM ranker, delivering 227 bps mean AP lift across five seeds, validated with leave-one-out ablations and leakage checks.

Built a mixture-of-experts ranker with 15 specialist LightGBM models and a learned per-rider gate. Reached 322 bps AP lift in a single offline study; selected a consolidated 271-bps model for production latency constraints.

Unblocked a Spark feature pipeline stalled for seven weeks by tracing driver OOMs to insufficient heap memory, then tuning driver memory, shuffle partitions, dynamic allocation, and adaptive coalescing.

Worked on search, personalization, and recommendation for consumer-facing agents. Connected conversational buyer memory to user profiles with evaluation and distillation quality loops across Rails, GraphQL, gRPC, and LLM orchestration.
Shipped 22 production PRs in 15 days across features, resiliency, and performance; delivered a four-month Agentic Buyer Persona roadmap in under 10 days with fewer than 12,000 lines of code.

Engineered an agentic EDA-to-ETL pipeline over workforce data in PySpark with MLflow, Optuna, ensemble calibration, Airflow, and Kafka. Co-authored an MCP-based SDK across 50+ workflows, reducing variance 27% and RMSE 8% at 99.95% SLA and sub-100ms latency.
Contributed to proprietary research on econometric clustering of talent-signal embeddings, with PyMC/Statsmodels calibration, DVC tracking, and Kubernetes inference.

Architected an alpha-signal retrieval pipeline on Databricks with Delta Lake, Spark, asynchronous multi-stage retrieval, and Azure OpenAI Batch with Claimification. Reached 99% entailment, 97.8% accuracy, and 96.4% macro-F1 across 3,000+ questions per batch.
Built Scala retrieval optimization with MLlib MinHashLSH deduplication and learned query routing, reducing cross-retriever collisions 58% and latency from 20 minutes to 3 minutes.

Shipped an internal multi-tenant RAG chat over Pinecone namespaces, indexing SharePoint and ServiceNow. Delivered GitHub Actions CI/CD, RAGAS evaluations, Unsloth QLoRA fine-tuning, and OpenTelemetry, cutting release time 60%.

experiences.organization: E.J. Pratt Library, University of Toronto
bullets: Built a version-controlled scheduling system with a Random Forest optimizer and an OAuth-secured ticketing REST API using MongoDB and Redis, improving shift coverage 12% and reducing resolution time 40% (3 days to 1.8 days).

research.organization: PMCC AI Lab, University Health Network · Vector Institute
bullets: Statistical imaging: developed theory and likelihood methods for recovering junction geometry under unknown blur, with identifiability and minimax guarantees and evaluations on single-molecule microscopy and Chandra X-ray spectra.
LLM evaluation: developed simultaneous confidence bands and sample-efficient audits for test-time scaling curves, covering best-of-k selection, pass@k, and majority voting.

Computational genomics: co-developed an auditable agentic variant-to-gene pipeline with recorded evidence retrieval; benchmarked gene rankings and used ablations to distinguish recall of known associations from use of retrieved evidence.

publications.title: An auditable agentic pipeline for variant-to-gene prioritisation, validated against orthogonal functional evidence
publications.authors: Shakuntala Baichoo, Sohail (Neel) Sarkar, Bo Wang
publications.summary: Evaluates an auditable variant-to-gene pipeline against functional evidence. Ablations distinguish gains from recall of known gene associations from gains due to the retrieved evidence.
publications.researchGroup: PMCC AI Lab, University Health Network

publications.title: Junction Geometry Survives an Unidentifiable Blur
publications.summary: Studies recovery of junction arm counts and directions despite unknown Gaussian-mixture blur, with statistical guarantees and evaluations on microscopy localizations and X-ray spectra.
publications.researchGroup: PMCC AI Lab, University Health Network

publications.title: Polygons and coplanar points on submanifolds of codimension 2
publications.summary: Proves that smooth codimension-two submanifolds in dimensions n ≥ 6 contain affinely regular pentagons locally, addressing Problem 73 on Green’s list. Extends the argument to prime-sided polygons.

publications.title: Cheap to Draw, Expensive to Trust: Certifying Test-Time Scaling Curves
publications.summary: Develops simultaneous confidence bands and sample-efficient audits for test-time scaling curves, accounting for budget selection and differences between benchmark questions.
publications.researchGroup: PMCC AI Lab, University Health Network

publications.title: Coherent Swap Regret and Channel-Proof Learning
publications.summary: Introduces coherent swap regret against local CPTP deviations in quantum games, with an O(√(dT log d)) algorithm via entropic mirror ascent.

publications.title: Visibility Cliques, Cubic Containers, and Dense Orchard Cores
publications.summary: Proves quantitative cases of the Big-Line–Big-Clique Conjecture in structured geometric regimes using cubic containers and dense orchard cores. The full conjecture remains open.

description: Built a bare-metal OS in Rust where an LLM is the kernel, booting through UEFI/USB and running a Gemma 4 E2B forward pass with int4 weights.
Implemented a Turbo-Quant QJL-compressed KV cache (approximately 9× key and 13× value compression), validated by 109 tests across five crates.
Built a context-compression layer encoding chunks into dense vectors, with reinforcement learning policies that expand high-value spans under token budgets.
Achieved 67% token reduction and 3× throughput while preserving QA accuracy, validated through ablations and metric-driven evaluations.
Built a Rust ML compiler with MLIR-based intermediate representation, three kernel variants, auto-tuning, and CPU/GPU backends.
Implemented an LLM inference pipeline with KV cache and RoPE, a benchmarking suite, and Cerebras API integration.
Built a searchless chess engine reported at approximately 2500 Elo, using multi-task Q-value distillation from Stockfish.
Trained on 70M+ positions and optimized inference to under 100ms per move with INT8 quantization and ONNX export.
